messages:
Anya: Quick sync — I'm proposing we retire the /v1/envelopes endpoint in favor of a flatter /generate route. Need a practical cutover plan that covers client cohorting, CDN cache keying, and a short-lived server-side unwrapping shim. cc @Ravi @Ben
Ravi: +1. What's the minimum server-side compatibility we can keep during cutover? My worry is a big chunk of mobile/web clients still expect framed envelopes at the CDN edge.
Ben: My suggestion: ship a server-side unwrapping shim that stays active for a defined window (2 weeks). Clients opt into a cohort header so we can measure behavior, then remove the shim. Also keep long-tail telemetry for 6 months to find stragglers.
Sarah: Which header are we adding? We have X-Client-Version but that's noisy and not explicit for frame format.
Ravi: Proposed header: `X-Redwood-Client-Cohort: envelope-v1/alpha` — explicit, pluggable. SDKs (JS/Python/Go) can set it automatically, so apps don't need manual changes.
Anya: Perfect. On the CDN side: plan to include cohort header in the cache key. For alpha cohort set short TTL (10m) so we can iterate quickly. Default unknown clients keep 1h TTL to avoid regressing latency. This will let us observe errors quickly without sweeping invalidation.
Max: Observability plan: add a boolean request tag `compat.envelope_v1` and a per-tenant gauge `compat.stragglers_by_tenant`. Create an alert if >1% of requests for a tenant hit the shim after 7 days. Also log a compact failure fingerprint when envelope-unwrapping fails.
Ben: About fallback behavior — can we auto-fallback to the unwrapping shim when we detect malformed JSON? That might help older mobile clients.
Sarah: Auto-fallback adds latency and complexity. If we do it, make it sampling-based (1% by default) and only for requests under a token threshold. Avoid doing heavy fallback on hot paths.
Anya: Agreed. Sampling fallback only, with a runtime flag we can toggle per-service. Action items: 1) Ravi -> PR to SDKs to emit header (ETA Wed EOD). 2) Max -> telemetry + alert + runbook. 3) Ben -> CDN cache-key patch and TTL config. 4) Anya -> deprecation draft + RFC follow-up doc.
Ravi: Rollout cohorts: alpha (10% tenant selector) -> beta (50%) -> global. Gate on `compat.envelope_v1/active` metric and the shim-error-rate. If shim-error-rate spikes, rollback the cohort.
deploy-bot: deployment queued: service/redwood-api v2026.04.12 -> staging at 2026-04-12T15:12:00Z
Anya: Sounds good. I'll start the follow-up doc and wire the tasks in the sprint board. If anyone has strong objections to the sampling-fallback or TTL numbers speak up now. :rocket:
